item.title: Chapter 3, Part 2 – Runtime Environment & Error Detection
item.description:
Runtime Environment

The space allocation for programs and data in memory during execution.

There are 3 types:

1. Fully-Static Environment

All properties of the language are predetermined before execution. Address allocation happens when the code is loaded, not when it runs.

FORTRAN is the classic example. All variable memory locations are fixed during execution. FORTRAN also only has one type of procedure, the subroutine, and subroutines can’t be nested. This also rules out recursion. So the original FORTRAN fits a fully-static environment well.

item.title: Chapter 3, Part 3 – Programming Languages Domains
item.description:
Programming languages are generally split into several domains based on their use case.

Domain Description Example Languages
Scientific Applications with a computational base. Where programming originally started. FORTRAN, C, ALGOL60
Business Applications for commercial use, especially banking. Came after the scientific domain. COBOL (and database languages), JAVA
Artificial Intelligence Languages built for AI work LISP, PROLOG
Systems Programming Programming all aspects of the computer, including hardware Machine Language, Assembly, C
Very High Level Languages Essentially scripting languages Python, Bash
